title: RECOVER TABLE versus an already loaded delete-range task

payload.p_check: RECOVER removes the persistent mysql.gc_delete_range row
payload.q_claim: a successful RECOVER leaves no executor authorized to destroy the republished physical table ID
payload.owner_red: a manually loaded stale task deletes all 32 recovered rows and all 32 index entries
payload.production_guard: GC prepare commits tikv_gc_safe_point before deleteRanges; RECOVER either disables GC first or rejects a snapshot older than that point
payload.stop_rule: do not classify as a bug unless a real GC path loads an eligible task while RECOVER still accepts the same snapshot

name: Revalidate destructive task ownership after cancellation can race with execution

payload.pattern: a durable task row is copied into an executor, a recovery or cancellation path removes the row, and the executor can later perform an irreversible action
matrix_dimensions: final ownership check present or absent
oracle_gate: preserve a preimage aggregate outside the target range
read from a fresh session after the destructive action
admission_gate: prove the executor input is generated by the production scheduler
prove every global frontier or lease checked by recovery is mutually compatible

name: Successful table recovery revokes every delete-range executor for the recovered physical ID

payload.p_check: RECOVER TABLE returns success and republishes the historical table ID
payload.q_claim: no delete-range task can subsequently remove that table's row or index keyspace
payload.owner_counterexample: task loaded before RECOVER and resumed after persistent task removal
payload.production_result: counterexample state is blocked by the GC safe-point and GC-enable transaction interlock

name: Owner-level RED followed by production reachability admission

steps: use a strong persisted terminal oracle
enumerate guards shared by producer and competing operation
solve the timestamp and lock constraints together
classify RED only if the constraints are satisfiable
payload.anti_pattern: treating a unit-test helper argument as if the production scheduler could emit it
payload.result_here: manual max safe point contradicted the persisted safe point accepted by RECOVER

environment.nonproduction_input: MockGCWorker.DeleteRanges(math.MaxInt64) while mysql.tidb safe point remains before DROP

lessons.classification: real destructive owner defect under an impossible scheduler state; not a product bug
lessons.oracle: preimage aggregate is required because complete row-plus-index range loss remains structurally consistent

code_ref.counterfactual: reload eligible tasks after the pause and before physical destruction

lessons.selector_precision: the exact owner counterfactual closes the owner-level RED
lessons.fix_note: a robust production design would need an atomic claim, lease, or epoch rather than a racy standalone re-read

ordering: GC prepare transaction checks enable and commits the new tikv_gc_safe_point
GC waits, resolves locks, then calls deleteRanges with that same point
RECOVER disables GC and validates its snapshot against persisted tikv_gc_safe_point
evidence.constraint: an eligible drop task has task_ts below the committed point, so RECOVER of that historical snapshot cannot succeed after GC preparation

lessons.method: owner RED is necessary but insufficient; solve the scheduler and recovery guards as one constraint system before bug admission
lessons.stop_rule: retire this exact candidate unless a distinct producer bypasses the interlock
